strings.name: Thabo Mbeki
strings.summary: An anti-apartheid activist and economist, Mbeki became deputy president in 1994 and president in 1999. He promoted African cooperation, but HIV/AIDS skepticism and treatment delays gravely damaged his public-health legacy. Resigning in 2008, he remained active; in 2026 he denied obstructing apartheid-era prosecutions at a public inquiry.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His presidency, African development and mediation, and economic and health policies had major historical influence.
